frase_gancho.texto: In the Alcázar, two eras lived side by side: the residence of Maximilian and Carlota, and the home of the presidents who came after.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: The Alcázar is the part of the castle whose occupants changed most often. Maximilian and Carlota lived here between eighteen sixty-four and eighteen sixty-seven. The architect Ramón Rodríguez Arangoity adapted the building as a palace, and the Alcázar took on the appearance it keeps today. After the fall of the empire, it became a residence for presidents. An INAH article records that in eighteen seventy-two, under Sebastián Lerdo de Tejada, it was designated as the presidential residence. The museum’s wall labels tell us that Manuel González opened an interior staircase. They also tell us that Porfirio Díaz used it mostly in summer, because his family lived on La Cadena Street. The museum describes twenty-two halls in the Alcázar. The ground floor recalls above all Maximilian and Carlota, and the upper floor recalls Díaz and his wife, Carmen Romero Rubio. Lázaro Cárdenas brought the presidential era to an end when he moved to Los Pinos.
